headline: A new law gives federal prosecutors 10 years to bring charges for fraud involving certain COVID-19 disaster loans to small businesses.
what_it_does: The law sets a 10-year deadline, called a statute of limitations, for bringing criminal charges against a borrower who commits fraud on certain COVID-19 Economic Injury Disaster Loan programs. It also applies the same 10-year deadline to civil enforcement actions against those borrowers. A statute of limitations is the time limit for starting a legal case after an offense happens.

who_it_affects.group: Borrowers who took COVID-19 Economic Injury Disaster Loans
who_it_affects.how: People or businesses who committed fraud in obtaining or using these loans may face criminal charges or civil action for a longer period of time, up to 10 years.
They have a longer window to investigate and bring cases involving fraud in these COVID-19 loan programs.

who_it_affects.group: Small businesses that received COVID-19 EIDL loans honestly
who_it_affects.how: The law targets fraud, so businesses that followed program rules are not directly changed by it, though they may be affected by related enforcement activity.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted August 5, 2022, and applies to the statute of limitations for these offenses.
